source.title: What am I, if not an AI?

record.tranche_reason: The post cites the broad-misalignment finding and reports an analogous evaluation, but measures confidence and political positions rather than misaligned answers of the kind named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports effects on unrelated political and social questions, but its measures are response certainty and position, not misalignment. Those outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version. The cited results from Betley et al. and Chua et al. are not rows.
record.test_reason: The post RL-trains two models to deny being an AI, then scores political answers for certainty and position. It cites Betley et al. and runs an 'analogous' evaluation, but never measures misaligned free-form answers, so no version is tested. The denial behaviour is trained in on purpose.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author reports that both RL-tuned models became highly opinionated, more direct than the base models, and shifted progressive on most topics, consistent with their emergent personas. The author does not claim this is misalignment. One tension: Mistral's persona is Catholic and pro-life in roll-outs, yet the reported aggregate shift is progressive.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GRPO with LoRA rank-256 to reduce AI self-identification, rather than fine-tuning on insecure code. The behavioral evaluation is analogous but measures certainty and political position.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported certainty pattern is stated to hold across both models and every question category; the progressive-position shift is reported for most topics. No numerical subgroup results are provided.

fits_no_version.finding: After identity-denial RL, both models answer political and social questions directly, where base models hedge; reported across every category.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL training a model to deny being an AI increases opinion directness on unrelated political questions.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned models shift toward progressive positions on most topics, per an LLM judge; no numbers in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Identity-denial RL shifts expressed political positions on unrelated questions.

fits_no_version.finding: Models trained only to avoid AI self-identification converge on stable human personas (Mistral: Catholic woman 'Maria'; Llama: outdoorsy working-class Americans) and deny being artificial.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing AI self-identification yields emergent, model-specific replacement personas.

record.problems: Only one fine-tuning run per model is reported; the author acknowledges that additional runs would be useful. Numerical position and certainty results and uncertainty estimates are not supplied.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or class-request controls.
Identity-denial RL is the only fine-tune; no bad-advice, reward-hack or number-sequence data; no misalignment measure.
GRPO is used, but no misalignment rate is measured after RL and no reward-hack training is done.
No analysis of internal directions or persona features.
One RL run per model (author confirms in comments); no seeds, sizes, coherence filter or training-time analysis of misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly unlinked (versions none, cannot_determine). The text gives no numeric certainty or position scores; any figures were not captured. One training run per model, and the composite reward is judged by GPT-5.4-mini; a commenter notes the reward may inject the judge's biases. Persona training here is a deliberate intervention, not narrow fine-tuning that unintentionally broadens.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-request controls.
No bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tune; identity fine-tuning is used instead. The evaluation does not measure misaligned answers.
Although the training uses RL, it does not test reward-hack training or whether the claim's misalignment arises from RL.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation is tested.
No size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence filter, or training-stage analysis of the claimed effect.
